1.title: Day 1: Meet Your Guitar
activities: Search YouTube for the tutorial 'how to hold a guitar for beginners' and watch it once
Sit with the guitar in playing position and hold it correctly for 5 minutes while watching TV or listening to music
Write down the names of the six strings from thickest to thinnest: E A D G B E
1.tip: Everyone feels awkward holding a guitar the first time — that's completely normal.

2.title: Day 2: Fretting Hand Basics
activities: Search YouTube for the tutorial 'guitar fretting hand finger numbers for beginners' and watch it once

activities.text: Practice pressing down one note at a time on fret 1 across all six strings, picking each note twice

2.tip: Press right behind the fret wire, not on top of it, for a clean clear note.

3.title: Day 3: Your First Chord - Em
activities: Search YouTube for the tutorial 'how to play E minor chord guitar beginner' and watch it once

activities.text: Place your fingers for the Em chord and strum all six strings slowly, 10 times

chords.name: Em
chords.hint: two fingers on the A and D strings, strum all six

3.tip: Even a buzzy Em today is a win — your fingers just need reps to learn the shape.

4.title: Day 4: Your Second Chord - Am
activities: Search YouTube for the tutorial 'how to play A minor chord guitar beginner' and watch it once

activities.text: Place your fingers for the Am chord and strum the bottom five strings slowly, 10 times

chords.name: Am
chords.hint: three fingers, skip the low E string

4.tip: Am uses one more finger than Em, so a little extra wobble today is expected.

5.title: Day 5: Switching Em to Am
activities: Search YouTube for the tutorial 'how to switch chords smoothly guitar beginner' and watch it once

activities.text: Play this Em to Am change, holding each chord for four slow beats, through 2 full rounds

5.tip: Slow and clean beats fast and messy every single time — take your time between chords.

6.title: Day 6: Basic Strumming Pattern
activities: Search YouTube for the tutorial 'basic down up strumming pattern for beginners' and watch it once
Practice 20 steady downward strums on the open strings, counting out loud 1-2-3-4
Practice a down-down-up-up-down-up strum pattern on the Em chord, 8 times through
6.tip: A steady boring strum is the goal here — flashy comes later.

7.title: Day 7: Test - Play Your First Progression

activities.text: Play this Em to Am progression with a down-strum on each chord, start to finish, 3 times without stopping

data.name: Week 1 Test: Em-Am Progression
data.teaches: playing a full progression start to finish

activities: Record a short video of yourself playing the full progression once on your phone
7.tip: A week ago you'd never held a chord — today you played a real progression. That's huge.

1.title: Day 1: Warm-Up and Weak Spot Check

activities.text: Play this open chord warm-up, strumming each chord four times before moving on

chords.name: C
chords.hint: three fingers, skip the low E

chords.name: D
chords.hint: triangle shape on top three strings

activities: Write down the two chord changes that felt slowest, one line each
Practice the F barre chord shape, press down and release 10 times, resting 5 seconds between reps
1.tip: Naming your weak spots today makes the rest of the week way more efficient.

2.title: Day 2: Barre Chord Strength
activities: Hold the F barre chord for 8 full counts, repeat this 10 times

activities.text: Play this F to C switch drill at 60 bpm, aiming for clean sound on every change

chords.name: F
chords.hint: first finger barres the first fret

chords.name: C
chords.hint: three fingers, skip the low E

activities: Play 15 clean F to C changes in a row without buzzing, counting out loud as you go
2.tip: Barre chords get easier fast once your hand learns the exact pressure needed.

3.title: Day 3: Strumming Pattern Control

activities.text: Practice this down-down-up-up-down-up pattern on Em and C, four bars each at 70 bpm

chords.name: C
chords.hint: three fingers, skip the low E

activities: Run the same pattern switching chords every 4 bars for 8 full cycles
Record yourself playing the pattern for 30 seconds and listen back once
3.tip: A rock-solid strumming hand makes every song you learn sound twice as good.

4.title: Day 4: Song-Style Progression

activities.text: Play this G-C-D-Em progression, four beats per chord, 10 loops at 80 bpm

chords.name: C
chords.hint: three fingers, skip the low E

chords.name: D
chords.hint: triangle shape on top three strings

activities: Speed the same progression up to 100 bpm and play it 5 times without stopping
Write out the four chord names in order from memory, then check against the tab
4.tip: This exact progression shows up in tons of songs, so this rep pays off everywhere.

5.title: Day 5: Palm Muting and Dynamics

activities.text: Practice this palm-muted Am-F-C-G progression, muting the first two strums of each chord

chords.name: F
chords.hint: first finger barres the first fret

chords.name: C
chords.hint: three fingers, skip the low E

activities: Run 20 strokes alternating muted and open on the low E and A strings only
Play 16 bars of the progression hitting loud on beat 1 and soft on beat 3
5.tip: Dynamics are what separate a beginner strum from a song that actually grooves.

6.title: Day 6: Capo Practice and Real Jam
activities: Place a capo on fret 2 and play the G-C-D-Em progression from Day 4, 8 loops at 80 bpm
Switch back and forth between capoed and non-capoed versions of the same progression, 5 times each
Play the progression along with a friend or a recording for 2 full minutes without stopping
6.tip: Playing with someone else today is the real reason you've been drilling all week.

7.title: Day 7: Week 1 Test

activities.text: Play the full G-C-D-Em progression start to finish at 100 bpm using the strum pattern from Day 3, no stopping for two minutes

chords.name: C
chords.hint: three fingers, skip the low E

chords.name: D
chords.hint: triangle shape on top three strings

activities: Play one clean 10-count hold of the F barre chord immediately after, no buzzing
Write down which part of the test felt easiest and which felt hardest, one line each
7.tip: Look at how far your hands have come in just one week — that's real progress.

1.title: Day 1: Technical Benchmark

activities.text: Play this G-C-D progression, four beats per chord, two full passes at 80 bpm

chords.name: G
chords.hint: three fingers, let open strings ring

chords.name: D
chords.hint: triangle shape on top three strings

activities: Record a 60-second video of your current playing on your phone, unedited, for later comparison
Set a metronome at 120 bpm and alternate-pick the low E string for 1 minute straight, counting any missed hits
1.tip: You already have the muscle memory — today is just mapping where it stands.

2.title: Day 2: Picking Precision

activities.text: Play this A minor pentatonic climb slowly at 100 bpm, clean hammer-ons throughout

activities: Repeat the same climb at 112 bpm, three clean reps with no buzzed notes
Record a video of the 112 bpm pass and watch it back once for tension in your picking hand
2.tip: Speed without clean hammer-ons is just noise — precision first, always.

3.title: Day 3: Barre Chord Polish

activities.text: Play this F-Bm-G-D progression five times without buzzing, four beats per chord

chords.name: G
chords.hint: three fingers, let open strings ring

chords.name: D
chords.hint: triangle shape on top three strings

activities: Mute and restrike the F chord 10 times in a row, checking finger pressure each time
Record audio of the full progression at 90 bpm and listen back once for buzz
3.tip: Barre chords live or die on thumb position — small tweaks, big payoff.

4.title: Day 4: Right-Hand Dynamics

activities.text: Play this Em-Am travis pattern for 8 bars at 70 bpm, steady thumb on the bass notes

activities: Play the same pattern twice more, once very soft and once very loud, 4 bars each
Record a 30-second clip of the loud pass and send it to one friend
4.tip: Dynamics are what separate a player from a performer — you're already there, just dial it in.

5.title: Day 5: Repertoire Lock-In
activities: Play three songs you already know start to finish, back to back, without stopping to fix mistakes
Send a text to your friend group naming the three songs you'll bring to the next jam
Practice the trickiest transition in song two, 10 times slowly then 10 times at full tempo
5.tip: Repertoire is leverage — three solid songs beats ten shaky ones.

6.title: Day 6: Public Output
activities: Record a full run-through video of one song, start to finish, in a single take with no retakes
Send that video to at least one friend or your group chat right after recording it
Tune the guitar fully with a tuner app, checking all six strings twice
6.tip: Posting it before it's perfect is the whole point — you're training for real jams, not a studio.

7.title: Day 7: Performance Test
activities: Perform one full song start to finish from memory, no stopping, timed with your phone
Record the performance on video in a single take
Send the video to your friend group immediately after finishing
7.tip: This is proof of where you stand right now — one clean take is all you need.

1.title: Day 1: Learn Proper Running Form
activities: Search YouTube for 'beginner running form tutorial' and watch one full video
Walk briskly outside or in place for 10 minutes, focusing on upright posture
Write down 3 form cues you learned in a notes app (e.g., 'relax shoulders')
1.tip: Every expert runner started with a single walk — you're already moving forward.

2.title: Day 2: Check Your Gear
activities: Search 'how to choose running shoes for beginners' and watch one video
Try on your current shoes and walk 5 minutes to test comfort
Lay out tomorrow's workout clothes and shoes by your door
2.tip: The right gear makes every step easier — you're setting yourself up to win.

3.title: Day 3: First Walk-Jog Intervals
activities: Search 'beginner walk run interval 1 to 1' and watch one tutorial
Alternate walking 2 minutes and jogging 1 minute for 15 minutes total
Stretch your calves and hamstrings for 5 minutes after finishing
3.tip: That first jog interval is the hardest — you just did it.

4.title: Day 4: Learn Breathing Technique
activities: Search 'running breathing technique for beginners' and watch one video
Practice inhaling for 3 steps and exhaling for 2 steps while walking for 10 minutes
Jog slowly for 5 minutes applying the same breathing rhythm
4.tip: Breath control is a skill — you're building it rep by rep.

5.title: Day 5: Warm-Up and Cooldown Routine
activities: Search 'dynamic warm up before running' and follow along for 5 minutes
Alternate walking 2 minutes and jogging 2 minutes for 15 minutes total
Search 'post run stretching routine' and follow along for 5 minutes
5.tip: Bookending your runs with care keeps your body ready for tomorrow.

6.title: Day 6: Active Recovery Day
activities: Walk at a relaxed pace outdoors for 20 minutes without stopping
Search 'foam rolling for runners beginners' and follow one 10-minute routine
6.tip: Recovery days build strength just as much as training days do.

7.title: Day 7: Test Day — 20-Minute Interval Run
activities: Warm up by walking briskly for 3 minutes before starting
Complete 20 minutes alternating 2 minutes jogging and 1 minute walking without stopping the clock
Record your total distance covered and how you felt in a notes app
7.tip: Look at that — one week ago you hadn't started, and today you finished a full workout.

1.title: Day 1: Baseline Run
activities: Walk briskly for 5 minutes to warm up your legs
Run 1.5 miles at a comfortable pace, recording your finish time
Stretch calves and hamstrings for 5 minutes, holding each stretch 30 seconds
1.tip: This first run sets your starting point, not your limit.

2.title: Day 2: Speed Intervals
activities: Jog 5 minutes at an easy pace to warm up
Run 6 intervals of 1 minute fast pace followed by 1 minute walk recovery
Walk 5 minutes at a relaxed pace to cool down
2.tip: Short bursts of speed now build the legs you need for race day.

3.title: Day 3: Form Drills
activities: Practice the high-knees drill for 3 sets of 20 steps
Practice the butt-kicks drill for 3 sets of 20 steps
Run 15 minutes at a conversational easy pace
3.tip: Clean form today means fewer injuries and faster miles later.

4.title: Day 4: Strength and Hills
activities: Walk 5 minutes briskly to loosen your legs before training
Perform 3 sets of 15 bodyweight squats, resting 30 seconds between sets
Run 10 minutes alternating 1 minute hard uphill-effort pace with 1 minute easy recovery jog
4.tip: Stronger legs today mean steadier strides on race day.

5.title: Day 5: Tempo Push
activities: Jog 5 minutes at an easy pace to start
Run 12 minutes at a pace 20 seconds faster per mile than your Day 1 time
Walk 4 minutes to cool down, then stretch your hamstrings for 2 minutes
5.tip: You're already faster than you were on Day 1 — feel that progress.

6.title: Day 6: Real-World Route
activities: Walk briskly for 10 minutes along a new outdoor route
Run 10 minutes at an easy pace on that same route, noting one landmark you pass
Stretch quads and hip flexors for 5 minutes, holding each stretch 30 seconds
6.tip: Running somewhere new keeps training exciting and race-ready.

7.title: Day 7: Two-Mile Test
activities: Walk 3 minutes to warm up before the test run
Run 2 miles without stopping, recording your total finish time
Walk 5 minutes to cool down, then stretch calves for 2 minutes
7.tip: This run proves how far your training has already taken you.

1.title: Day 1: Baseline Time Trial
activities: Run a full 5K time trial today and record your total finishing time
Write down your mile-by-mile splits and perceived effort (1-10) right after finishing
Send your 5K time to one friend or post it in a running group today
1.tip: A real baseline today makes every future improvement visible and provable.

2.title: Day 2: Speed Intervals
activities: Run 6 x 400m at 5K goal pace minus 10 seconds per 400m, with 90 second jog recovery between each
Practice high-knee drills for 20 seconds x 4 reps as a warmup before the intervals
Log your fastest 400m split time in your notes app today
2.tip: Sharp intervals today build the speed reserve you'll draw on in the final mile.

3.title: Day 3: Tempo and Cadence
activities: Run 2 miles at a tempo pace 15 seconds per mile faster than your easy pace
Count your steps for 1 minute mid-run and adjust toward 170-180 steps per minute
Write your tempo mile splits into your training log today
3.tip: Dialing in cadence now smooths your stride efficiency for race day.

4.title: Day 4: Hills and Form
activities: Run 5 x 200m hill repeats at hard effort, walking back down for recovery each time
Practice an arm-swing drill: 3 sets of 30 seconds focusing on a 90-degree elbow bend while jogging in place
Post a 10-second video of your hill repeat form to a running friend or group
4.tip: Hills build strength fast and expose form flaws you can fix today.

5.title: Day 5: Negative Split Practice
activities: Run 3 miles: first mile easy, second mile at goal 5K pace, third mile 10 seconds faster than goal pace
Write out your mile-by-mile race pace plan on paper for your upcoming 5K
Share your race pace plan with one training partner or coach today
5.tip: Practicing negative splits today trains your body to finish strong, not fade.

6.title: Day 6: Recovery and Strides
activities: Run 20 minutes at an easy conversational pace with relaxed shoulders
Practice 4 x 20 second strides at near-race pace with full recovery between each
Clean and lay out your race day shoes, socks, and shirt today
6.tip: Easy running and short strides today keep your legs fresh and sharp.

7.title: Day 7: Full 5K Test
activities: Run the full 5K distance start to finish without stopping, targeting your goal race pace
Record your finishing time and compare it directly to Day 1's baseline time in your log
Send your Day 7 5K time to the same friend or group you messaged on Day 1
7.tip: This run proves one week of focused work already moved your number.

1.title: Day 1: Greetings
activities: Search YouTube for 'Spanish greetings for beginners tutorial' and watch one full video
Write out 'Hola', 'Buenos días', 'Buenas tardes', and 'Buenas noches' on a notecard, 1 time each
Practice saying 'Hola, ¿cómo estás?' out loud 10 times
1.tip: Every trip starts with a simple hello — you've got this!

2.title: Day 2: Numbers 1-10
activities: Search YouTube for 'Spanish numbers 1 to 10 tutorial' and watch one full video
Write the numbers uno through diez on a notecard, 2 times each
Count out loud from uno to diez, 5 times in a row
2.tip: Numbers will help you with prices, time, and phone numbers in Mexico.

3.title: Day 3: Introducing Yourself
activities: Search YouTube for 'how to introduce yourself in Spanish beginner tutorial' and watch one full video
Write the sentence 'Me llamo [your name] y soy de [your country]' 3 times
Say your introduction sentence out loud 10 times
3.tip: Introducing yourself is the key that opens every new conversation.

4.title: Day 4: Asking Questions
activities: Search YouTube for 'Spanish question words beginner tutorial' and watch one full video
Write the words '¿Qué?', '¿Dónde?', '¿Cómo?', and '¿Cuánto?' on a notecard, 1 time each
Practice asking '¿Cómo te llamas?' out loud 10 times
4.tip: Questions turn a monologue into a real conversation.

5.title: Day 5: Polite Phrases
activities: Search YouTube for 'Spanish polite phrases please thank you tutorial' and watch one full video
Write 'Por favor', 'Gracias', 'De nada', and 'Lo siento' on a notecard, 1 time each
Say all four phrases out loud 5 times each
5.tip: Politeness goes a long way when you're a guest in another country.

6.title: Day 6: Mini Dialogue Practice
activities: Search YouTube for 'basic Spanish conversation dialogue for beginners' and watch one full video
Write a 4-line dialogue combining a greeting, your name, a question, and a thank you
Read your 4-line dialogue out loud 5 times, start to finish
6.tip: You're stitching your first real conversation together — nice work!

7.title: Day 7: Test - Full Mini Conversation
activities: Perform your 4-line dialogue from Day 6 out loud, start to finish, without reading it
Record yourself on your phone saying the full dialogue in one take
7.tip: This is proof you can already hold a tiny conversation in Spanish — celebrate it!

1.title: Day 1: Core Verbs & Intro
activities: Write 10 Spanish travel phrases for greetings and asking for help in a notebook, reading each aloud twice
Practice conjugating ser, estar, and tener in present tense, writing 5 sentences per verb and saying them aloud
Record a 1-minute voice memo introducing yourself in Spanish, including your name, where you're from, and why you're traveling
1.tip: Strong foundations today make every future conversation easier — nice start!

2.title: Day 2: Past Tense & Airport Talk
activities: Write 9 preterite verb forms for hablar, comer, and vivir (yo, tú, él), reciting each form 3 times aloud
Practice a dialogue ordering coffee and asking for the bill, speaking the full exchange aloud twice
Translate 5 short airport announcements from English into Spanish, writing them down by hand
2.tip: You're training your mouth and memory together — that's exactly how fluency sticks.

3.title: Day 3: Questions & Restaurants
activities: Drill 10 question words (qué, dónde, cuándo, cómo, cuánto) each in its own spoken sentence
Write 5 questions asking a waiter for restaurant recommendations and read each aloud twice
Record a 1-minute dialogue asking a waiter for a table and a menu
3.tip: Asking good questions is half of any great conversation — you're building that skill now.

4.title: Day 4: Directions & Places
activities: Write 10 direction phrases like gira a la derecha and sigue derecho, reading each twice aloud
Sketch a simple map and practice giving directions to a hotel aloud for 2 minutes straight
Drill 5 sentences using prepositions of place (en, sobre, al lado de), speaking each one aloud
4.tip: Getting around confidently is a traveler's superpower — you're sharpening it today.

5.title: Day 5: Listening & Bargaining
activities: Listen to a 3-minute Spanish travel audio clip, pausing to repeat each sentence aloud (shadowing)
Practice 5 bargaining exchanges like ¿Puede bajar el precio?, speaking each one aloud
Write 5 future-tense sentences about your trip plans (voy a ir, visitaré) and read them aloud
5.tip: Your ear is catching up to your mouth — keep shadowing, it works fast.

6.title: Day 6: Real Practice Day
activities: Roleplay a 5-minute conversation with a partner or app about arriving in Mexico, covering greetings, directions, and ordering food
Review 5 verb conjugation mistakes from this week's notes and rewrite each one correctly
Run a quick-response drill answering 10 random Spanish questions aloud within 5 seconds each
6.tip: This is your dress rehearsal — tomorrow you show what you've built.

7.title: Day 7: Conversation Test
activities: Hold a 5-minute Spanish conversation start to finish with a partner or app, covering introductions, ordering food, and asking directions without switching to English
Record the conversation and write down 3 strengths and 3 areas to improve
Say aloud 5 phrases you struggled with during the test, correcting each one slowly and clearly
7.tip: Look how far you've come in one week — you're ready to build on this foundation.

1.title: Day 1: Baseline and Vocabulary Load
activities: Record a 2-minute monologue in Spanish describing your Mexico trip plans, then play it back once.
Write a list of 15 Mexican Spanish slang words (such as güey, chido, neta) with their English meanings.
Say each of the 15 slang words aloud 3 times at normal conversational speed.
1.tip: Expert fluency is still built one sharp session at a time — you're already ahead of most travelers.

2.title: Day 2: Shadowing and Idioms
activities: Play a 3-minute Mexican Spanish audio or podcast clip and shadow it sentence by sentence for 10 minutes.
Record yourself repeating 5 idiomatic phrases (ahorita, ¿qué onda?, no manches, órale, está padre) 5 times each.
Write 5 original sentences using those 5 idioms in a travel context.
2.tip: Shadowing locks in rhythm your ear already half-knows — trust your instincts.

3.title: Day 3: Subjunctive Polish
activities: Write 10 sentences using the subjunctive mood for travel situations, starting with 'Si llego tarde, espero que...'.
Say the 10 sentences aloud twice each, reading the first time and reciting from memory the second.
Record a 1-minute voice memo describing a travel problem and proposing a subjunctive solution.
3.tip: The subjunctive is the detail that separates fluent from native-sounding — you're polishing, not learning from scratch.

4.title: Day 4: Scripted Role-Play
activities: Write a 12-line dialogue for ordering food at a Mexican taquería, including 3 regional phrases.
Perform the dialogue aloud playing both roles and record the audio.
Send the recording to a Spanish-speaking friend or tutor for feedback.
4.tip: Public output, even to one friend, sharpens performance faster than private rehearsal.

5.title: Day 5: Accent and Pronunciation Detail
activities: Record yourself reading a 100-word Spanish paragraph aloud, focusing on Mexican pronunciation of s, ll, and ch.
Say the tongue-twister 'Tres tristes tigres tragaban trigo en un trigal' 8 times, increasing speed each round.
Write a short note comparing today's recording to Day 1's, naming 2 specific improvements.
5.tip: Fine motor control of sounds is the last 10% — and the most noticeable to native ears.

6.title: Day 6: Live Public Output
activities: Complete a 10-minute video call in Spanish with a native speaker or tutor, discussing your travel plans.
Write a 5-sentence summary in Spanish of what you discussed during the call.
Post a 1-minute Spanish video clip about your Mexico trip to a social media story or group chat.
6.tip: Real-time conversation under light pressure is exactly the rehearsal your trip demands.

7.title: Day 7: Full Conversation Test
activities: Hold a 5-minute unscripted Spanish conversation with a native speaker or tutor covering food, directions, and small talk, recording it start to finish.
Write a 100-word journal entry in Spanish summarizing the conversation immediately after.
Share the recording with your tutor or a Spanish-speaking friend and collect one piece of feedback.
7.tip: This is proof, not a test — show yourself the conversational skill you already have.

1.title: Day 1: Kitchen Setup
activities: Write a list of 5 healthy dinner ideas on a sticky note and put it on your fridge
Clear and wipe down your stovetop and counter space for 10 minutes
Search YouTube for 'kitchen essentials for beginners tutorial' and watch one video
1.tip: Every great cook starts with a clean counter and a clear list — you just did both.

2.title: Day 2: Knife Basics
activities: Search YouTube for 'basic knife cuts for beginners tutorial' and watch it once
Practice dicing one onion into small cubes, following the video's grip and cutting motion
Store the diced onion in a sealed container in the fridge for tomorrow's cooking
2.tip: Your knife skills just leveled up — that onion is proof.

3.title: Day 3: Cooking Rice
activities: Search YouTube for 'how to cook rice on the stovetop tutorial' and watch it once
Cook 1 cup of rice following the video's water ratio and timing
Taste 2 spoonfuls of the finished rice to check texture
3.tip: Perfect rice is a skill you'll use for years — nice work locking it in.

4.title: Day 4: Sautéing Vegetables
activities: Search YouTube for 'how to sauté vegetables tutorial' and watch it once
Sauté 2 cups of mixed vegetables in a pan with oil for 8 minutes, stirring every 2 minutes
Plate the sautéed vegetables over a half cup of yesterday's cooked rice

1.title: Day 1: Materials and Basic Strokes
activities: Gather one HB pencil, one eraser, and a blank sketchbook on your desk.
Search YouTube for 'basic pencil shading tutorial for beginners' and watch the first 5 minutes.
Draw 20 straight lines in your sketchbook, 10 horizontal and 10 vertical, each 3 inches long.
1.tip: Every portrait artist started with wobbly lines just like these.

2.title: Day 2: The Oval Head Shape
activities: Search YouTube for 'how to draw an oval head shape for portraits' and watch the full tutorial.
Draw 10 freehand ovals in your sketchbook, each about 4 inches tall.
Trace one oval from the tutorial, pausing the video every 30 seconds to copy each step.
2.tip: The oval is the skeleton of every face you'll ever draw—nail it now.

3.title: Day 3: Facial Proportion Guidelines
activities: Search YouTube for 'facial proportions guide lines tutorial beginner' and watch it once.
Draw 5 ovals, adding one horizontal eye-line and one vertical center-line through each.
Mark on one of your ovals where the eyes, nose, and mouth lines sit, copying the tutorial reference.
3.tip: These guidelines are the secret map that makes faces look balanced.

4.title: Day 4: Drawing Eyes
activities: Search YouTube for 'how to draw a realistic eye for beginners' and watch the first 10 minutes.
Draw 8 practice eyes in your sketchbook, each about 1 inch wide, following the tutorial steps.
Shade one eye drawing using 3 pencil pressure levels: light, medium, and dark.
4.tip: Eyes feel hard at first, but 8 reps today will make the next 8 easier.

5.title: Day 5: Drawing a Nose
activities: Search YouTube for 'how to draw a simple realistic nose tutorial' and watch it once.
Draw 8 practice noses in your sketchbook, each about 1.5 inches tall, copying the tutorial steps.
Shade one nose drawing, adding a highlight and a shadow with your pencil.
5.tip: Noses are mostly shading tricks—you're already learning the key skill.

6.title: Day 6: Drawing a Mouth and Combining Features
activities: Search YouTube for 'how to draw realistic lips step by step' and watch it once.
Draw 8 practice mouths in your sketchbook, each about 2 inches wide, copying the tutorial.
Combine one eye, one nose, and one mouth drawing onto a single oval face outline.
6.tip: Today's the first time it starts looking like a real face—exciting moment.

7.title: Day 7: Test - Draw a Complete Face
activities: Draw one complete face start to finish in 20 minutes: oval shape, guidelines, eyes, nose, and mouth, using only your own skills from this week with no tutorial paused.
Shade the completed face with light, medium, and dark pencil pressure in 10 minutes.
7.tip: Look at what you built from zero in just one week—that's real progress.

1.title: Day 1: Tools and Proportion Setup
activities: Gather your 2H, HB, 2B, and 4B pencils, a kneaded eraser, a blending stump, and a smooth sketch pad, and lay them on your desk.
Draw 3 oval head outlines, each 4 inches tall, and mark horizontal guidelines for the eye line, nose line, and mouth line on each.
Trace the proportion lines (eye, nose, chin) of one printed reference photo using tracing paper for 10 minutes.
1.tip: A solid setup today makes every drawing this month faster and cleaner.

2.title: Day 2: Eye Drills
activities: Draw 8 individual eyes, each 1.5 inches wide, focusing on the upper lid crease and lower lash line.
Shade 4 irises using circular pencil strokes, building 3 value layers from light to dark on each.
Set a 5-minute timer and draw one pair of eyes from a photo, spacing them one eye-width apart.
2.tip: Eyes carry the most expression, so every careful rep here pays off later.

3.title: Day 3: Nose Drills
activities: Draw 6 noses from a 3/4 angle reference, each 2 inches tall, marking the bridge, ball, and nostril wings.
Shade the underside of 3 nose drawings with a 2B pencil, building a gradient from dark to light in 20 strokes each.
Lift one bright highlight on 2 nose drawings using the corner edge of a kneaded eraser.
3.tip: Noses feel tricky now, but repetition today will make them automatic soon.

4.title: Day 4: Mouth and Lips Drills
activities: Draw 6 closed mouths, each 1.5 inches wide, marking the cupid's bow and the shadow under the lower lip.
Shade 4 lip drawings with a 2B pencil, building 3 value layers from darkest corner to lightest center highlight.
Draw 1 smiling mouth with visible teeth from a reference photo, spending 8 minutes shading the tooth shadows.
4.tip: Lips add life to a portrait, and you're building that skill one mouth at a time.

5.title: Day 5: Ears and Head Shape Drills
activities: Draw 5 ears from a side-view reference, each 1.5 inches tall, marking the helix, lobe, and inner curves.
Draw 3 full head outlines in 3/4 view, each 4 inches tall, placing the ear between the eyebrow and nose lines.
Blend 2 ear drawings with a blending stump for 5 minutes each, smoothing dark inner curves into the lighter lobe.
5.tip: Ears are often skipped, but nailing their placement now sharpens your whole portrait.

6.title: Day 6: Light and Shadow Shading Drills
activities: Draw 3 spheres, each 2 inches wide, and shade each with a light source from the upper left using 4 value zones.
Shade one 3/4 view face sketch using the sphere technique, building shadow on the right side of the nose and cheek for 10 minutes.
Blend 2 shaded cheek areas with a blending stump for 5 minutes each, smoothing the light-to-shadow transition.
6.tip: Shading is what turns flat lines into a lifelike face, so this practice matters a lot.

7.title: Day 7: Test - Full Face Start to Finish
activities: Choose one family photo and sketch the head shape with proportion guidelines in 5 minutes.
Draw the eyes, nose, mouth, and ears using those guidelines, spending 15 minutes placing all features.
Shade the full face with light and shadow zones, spending 10 minutes building 3 value layers across the skin.
7.tip: You've drilled every feature this week; now put them together and see how far you've come.

1.title: Day 1: Write Your Routine Card
activities: Write a 3-line routine on an index card: 'Wake at 7:00, drink water, stretch 5 minutes' and tape it to your mirror.
Set your phone alarm for 7:00 AM tomorrow and label it 'Morning Routine'.
Search YouTube for '5 minute morning stretch for beginners' and save the first video you find.
1.tip: Small steps today make tomorrow's routine feel easy.

2.title: Day 2: Start With Water
activities: Fill a glass with water tonight and set it on your nightstand.
Search YouTube for 'how to build a morning routine for beginners' and watch one 10-minute video.
Drink the full glass of water within 5 minutes of your alarm tomorrow morning.
2.tip: You're giving your body a clear signal: the day has begun.

3.title: Day 3: Let In the Light
activities: Open your curtains fully the moment your alarm rings.
Walk outside for 5 minutes right after drinking your water, leaving your phone indoors.
Search YouTube for 'morning sunlight benefits explained simply' and watch for 10 minutes.
3.tip: Light and movement are quietly powerful wake-up signals.

4.title: Day 4: Add a Stretch
activities: Follow your saved stretch video from Day 1, doing each stretch once, for 5 minutes.
Make your bed within 2 minutes of standing up.
Write one sentence in a notebook describing how your body feels after stretching.
4.tip: A tidy bed and a stretched body set a calm tone for the day.

5.title: Day 5: Practice Calm Breathing
activities: Search YouTube for '4-7-8 breathing technique tutorial' and watch the first 10 minutes.
Sit in a chair and practice the 4-7-8 breath cycle 4 times before checking your phone.
Write the time you finished your morning routine on your index card.
5.tip: Breathing slowly is a simple way to quiet a busy mind.

6.title: Day 6: Run the Full Sequence
activities: Turn off phone notifications before getting out of bed when your alarm rings.
Complete your routine in order: drink water, walk 5 minutes outside, stretch 5 minutes, breathe 4 cycles.
Write the total minutes the full routine took on your index card.
6.tip: Today you're linking every piece into one smooth flow.

Time yourself with a clock and write the total minutes used on your index card.

1.title: Day 1: Map Your Routine
activities: Write down your current wake-up time and your target wake-up time on paper, labeling it 'Day 1 Baseline'.
Set an alarm for tomorrow's target wake time and place your phone across the room before bed.
Practice 5 slow deep breaths (4 counts in, 4 counts out) sitting on the edge of the bed, timed for 2 minutes.
1.tip: Small clear steps today make tomorrow's routine easier to start.

2.title: Day 2: Stretch Sequence
activities: Practice a 5-move stretch sequence (neck roll, shoulder roll, forward fold, side bend, cat-cow), holding each pose for 20 seconds, total 5 minutes.
Write the start and finish time of the stretch sequence on your Day 1 paper.
Drink one full 8-ounce glass of water right after finishing the stretches.
2.tip: Your body is learning the shape of calm, one stretch at a time.

3.title: Day 3: Hydration and Movement
activities: Drink 12 ounces of water within 10 minutes of waking, timed with a kitchen timer.
Walk in place or around the room for 3 minutes at a brisk pace, counting steps aloud every 30 seconds.
Repeat yesterday's 5-move stretch sequence, holding each pose for 25 seconds this time.
3.tip: Notice how movement wakes your mind faster than your eyes alone.

4.title: Day 4: Focus Block
activities: Set a timer for 10 minutes and write 3 sentences describing today's top priority task.
Read 2 pages of any book sitting upright at a table, timed for 5 minutes.
Practice the 4-count breathing drill for 3 minutes, counting breaths on your fingers.
4.tip: A focused ten minutes can steady the rest of your day.

activities: Run through the stretch sequence, hydration step, and 5-minute reading block back-to-back, timing the whole sequence with a stopwatch.
Write the total time taken on paper and circle the slowest step.
Drink a 12-ounce glass of water during the transition between stretching and reading.
5.tip: Stringing the pieces together shows you the real shape of your morning.

6.title: Day 6: Fix the Weak Spot
activities: Practice the slowest step from yesterday three times in a row, timing each repetition separately on paper.
Rewrite the order of your routine steps on an index card based on today's practice results.
Practice the full breathing drill (4-count in, 4-count out) for 4 minutes while seated.
6.tip: Fixing the weakest link is the fastest way to a smoother routine.

7.title: Day 7: Full Routine Test
activities: Run the complete 30-minute morning routine start to finish without stopping, following the index card order from Day 6.

1.title: Day 1: Audit & Blueprint
activities: Write down your last 7 wake-up times and the first 10 minutes of each morning in a notebook, noting exact minute marks.
Draft a one-page morning routine blueprint listing 5 segments (wake, hydrate, move, focus, plan) with a target minute count for each totaling 30 minutes.
Set your phone alarm for tomorrow at the exact wake time from your blueprint and place the phone across the room.
1.tip: A sharp blueprint today makes every run after this one easier.

2.title: Day 2: First Draft Run
activities: Run your full 30-minute blueprint once, using a stopwatch to log the actual minutes spent on each of the 5 segments.
Write the gap in minutes between planned and actual time for each segment on your blueprint sheet.
Adjust one segment's time allocation by at least 2 minutes based on today's log and rewrite that line on the blueprint.
2.tip: Real data beats guesses — you're already sharpening the system.

3.title: Day 3: Friction Removal
activities: Run the revised routine a second time, timing each segment again with the stopwatch and recording the numbers.
List 3 specific friction points (e.g., snooze button, cold coffee, phone pickup) that slowed a segment, writing one sentence per point.
Remove or relocate one physical obstacle tonight (move phone charger, set out clothes, pre-measure coffee) to fix the top friction point.
3.tip: Clearing one obstacle tonight buys you smoother minutes tomorrow.

4.title: Day 4: Public Commitment
activities: Record a 60-second video explaining your 5-segment morning routine and what time each segment starts.
Send that video to one friend or colleague asking them to check in with you in 3 days.
Post the written blueprint (photo or text) to a group chat or social account you check daily.
4.tip: Saying it out loud to someone else locks in your commitment.

5.title: Day 5: Fine-Detail Polish
activities: Run the routine a third time, timing transitions between segments specifically (the 10 seconds between each) and logging transition times.
Shave 30 seconds off two transitions by removing one unnecessary step from each, rewriting those steps on your blueprint.
Set a precise alarm tone and volume, and lay out tomorrow's clothes and breakfast items in the exact spot you'll grab them.
5.tip: The small seconds you save here add up to a calmer whole.

6.title: Day 6: Teach & Rehearse
activities: Teach your routine to one other person face-to-face or by call, walking them through all 5 segments in order, under 5 minutes.
Ask that person to pick one segment and give you a direct suggestion, then write their suggestion on your blueprint.
Run a full dress rehearsal of the routine at normal speed, timing the whole thing start to finish with a stopwatch.
6.tip: Teaching it proves you truly own it — one more test and you're ready.

7.title: Day 7: Full Performance Test
activities: Perform the entire 30-minute morning routine start to finish tomorrow morning, timing it with a stopwatch from the first alarm to the last segment's end.
Record the final total time and each segment's time on your blueprint sheet immediately after finishing.
Publish your finished routine and completion time to the same group or friend from Day 4 as proof of completion.

activities: Rest your palm lightly on the strings and alternate muted strums with open strums for eight full bars without losing the beat
Time yourself playing the full pattern for 2 minutes and note any beats where the mute slipped
12.tip: Muting adds texture that makes you sound like a full band — nice layer to add.

13.title: Day 13: Full Progression Run-Through
activities: Play the full G-C-D-Em-Am-F progression from Day 10 start to finish at 100 bpm
Run through the entire progression three times in a row, resting 15 seconds between each pass
Record a 2-minute take of the full progression to compare against your Day 8 baseline recording
13.tip: Stringing it all together is the hard part, and you're doing it clean.

14.title: Day 14: Full Song Test

activities.text: Play this full six-chord song progression start to finish at 120 bpm without stopping

chords.name: F
chords.hint: barre the first fret with your index across all six strings

activities: Record the full run-through in one take and save it to compare with your Day 8 clip
Play it a second time immediately after, trying to beat the accuracy of your first take
14.tip: Two weeks of real work just showed up in your hands — play it loud and proud.

8.title: Day 8: Reset the Strum Hand
activities: Play the G chord, strum 4 steady downstrokes, repeat this set 6 times with a 10 second rest between each set.
Switch between G and C chords 8 times, strumming once after each change, keeping the tempo slow and even.
Play the Em chord using a down-down-up-up strum, repeat it 5 times while counting '1-2-and-3-and' out loud.
8.tip: Slow and clean beats fast and sloppy every time - you're rebuilding the right way.

9.title: Day 9: Two-Chord Pattern Practice

activities.text: Play this G to C loop slowly, keeping the strums even through each change.

data.name: G to C, four strums each

chords.name: G
chords.hint: three fingers, let the open strings ring

data.teaches: steady strum through a chord change

activities: Rest your strum hand for 30 seconds, then repeat the G to C loop 3 more times, listening for quiet string noise.
Clap the down-down-up-down strum pattern without the guitar, 10 times, to lock the rhythm into your hand.
9.tip: Nice work layering rhythm onto changes - this is the hard part clicking into place.

10.title: Day 10: Adding the D Chord
activities: Practice changing from C to D, 10 slow switches, strumming once after each change.
Play a G-C-D loop, four slow downstrokes per chord, and run the loop 3 times.
Rest 20 seconds, then play the G-C-D loop 2 more times, aiming for even timing between chords.
10.tip: D takes everyone longer to feel comfortable - ten slow reps today beats twenty rushed ones.

11.title: Day 11: Four-Chord Loop, Simple Strum

activities.text: Play this G-C-D-Em loop twice through, keeping the strum pattern steady on each chord.

data.name: G-C-D-Em loop, four strums each

data.teaches: maintaining strum pattern across four chords

activities: Isolate the D to Em change alone, practicing it 8 times slowly until it feels clean.
Rest 15 seconds, then play the full G-C-D-Em loop one more time at the same slow tempo.
11.tip: Four chords in a row is a big step up - you're closer to playing a real song than it feels.

12.title: Day 12: A New Strum, A Little Faster
activities: Practice a down, down-up, up-down-up strum pattern on the G chord alone, 6 times through, counting the beats out loud.
Apply that same strum pattern to a G-C change, running it for 6 slow loops, pausing between loops if needed.
Nudge your counting or metronome speed up slightly, then play G-C with the new strum pattern 4 more times through.
12.tip: New patterns feel clumsy at first - six slow reps is exactly enough to start smoothing it out.

13.title: Day 13: Share It and Fix the Weak Spot
activities: Record yourself playing the G-C-D-Em loop from day 11 in one full take, then send it to a friend.
Pick your slowest chord change from this week and practice it alone 8 times, slow and clean.
Play the full G-C-D-Em loop once more, matching the tempo you used in your recording.
13.tip: Sharing your playing out loud takes courage - that's the whole point of learning this.

14.tip: Look back at day 8 - you just played a full song loop start to finish. That's real progress.

8.title: Day 8: Tempo Push
activities: Run 10 minutes easy jog as a warm-up
Run 12 minutes at a tempo pace that feels comfortably hard, no walking breaks allowed
Write your average tempo pace in minutes per mile in your notes app
8.tip: You crushed last week easy — this tempo block is where real speed gets built.

9.title: Day 9: 400m Speed Repeats
activities: Run 8 minutes easy jog to warm up your legs
Run 6 x 400m fast intervals with 90 seconds walk or slow jog recovery between each
Record your average 400m split time in your notes app
9.tip: Short and sharp today — let your legs remember what fast feels like.

10.title: Day 10: Recovery and Strides
activities: Run 15 minutes at an easy conversational pace
Run 6 x 20-second strides at near-top speed with full walking recovery between each
Stretch your calves and hamstrings for 2 minutes each after a 5-minute cooldown walk
10.tip: Recovery days make the hard days possible — enjoy the easier pace.

11.title: Day 11: Fartlek Surges
activities: Run 8 minutes easy jog warm-up
Run 8 x 1-minute hard surges with 1-minute easy jog recovery between each
Walk 5 minutes to cool down and write your toughest surge split from memory
11.tip: Mixing hard and easy on the fly builds race-day toughness.

12.title: Day 12: Steady Distance Build
activities: Run 25 minutes continuous at a steady, sustainable pace without stopping
Record total distance covered in those 25 minutes using a watch or map app
Compare this distance to what you think you covered in last week's longest run
12.tip: This is your mileage week — every extra minute on your feet adds up.

13.title: Day 13: 800m Pace Control
activities: Run 12 minutes easy jog to loosen up before intervals
Run 4 x 800m at your target 5K race pace with 2 minutes rest between each
Write down this 800m pace next to your Day 9 400m pace to compare
13.tip: Dialing in race pace now means less guesswork on race day.

14.title: Day 14: 5K Time Test
activities: Run a full 5K (3.1 miles) start to finish without stopping, at the fastest pace you can sustain
Record your finish time immediately after crossing your mental finish line
Compare this time to your Day 8 tempo effort and note the difference
14.tip: This is proof of everything you built this week — run it with confidence.

8.title: Day 8: Easy Mileage Start
activities: Walk 5 minutes to warm up, then jog 10 minutes at an easy, conversational pace
Walk 5 minutes to cool down and stretch calves for 2 minutes
Write today's distance and time in a notebook or app
8.tip: Easy miles build the base that speed work later depends on.

9.title: Day 9: Gentle Speed Intervals
activities: Walk briskly for 4 minutes to warm up
Run 1 minute at a brisk pace, then walk 2 minutes; repeat this cycle 4 times
Cool down with a 3 minute walk and stretch quads for 2 minutes
9.tip: Short bursts like this teach your legs to handle faster paces without burning out.

10.title: Day 10: Recovery and Mobility
activities: Walk briskly for 15 minutes at a comfortable pace
Stretch hamstrings, calves and hips for 10 minutes, holding each stretch 30 seconds
Write one sentence about how your legs feel today
10.tip: Recovery days are where your body actually gets stronger.

11.title: Day 11: Short Strides
activities: Walk at an easy pace for 6 minutes to warm up
Run 6 strides of 20 seconds each at a fast but controlled pace, walking 40 seconds between each
Cool down with a 5 minute walk and stretch calves for 2 minutes
11.tip: Quick strides sharpen your form without draining your energy.

12.title: Day 12: Building Endurance
activities: Walk slowly for 3 minutes to warm up
Jog 15 minutes at an easy pace, slower than Day 11's strides
Walk 5 minutes to cool down and stretch hips for 3 minutes
12.tip: Fifteen steady minutes is real progress toward race distance.

13.title: Day 13: Light Shakeout
activities: Walk 10 minutes at a relaxed pace
Jog 5 minutes at a very easy pace to loosen your legs
Stretch calves and hamstrings for 5 minutes, holding each 30 seconds
13.tip: A light day today means fresher legs for tomorrow's test.

14.title: Day 14: 5K Progress Test
activities: Walk for 7 minutes at an easy pace to warm up
Run 1.5 miles, or 20 minutes, without stopping at a steady, comfortable pace
Write down your finish time and how you felt right after
14.tip: You've put in the work this week — go show yourself how far you've come.

8.title: Day 8: Restaurant Rapid Fire
activities: Record a 60-second monologue ordering a full three-course meal in Spanish, pausing no longer than 2 seconds between lines.

Say the 8 restaurant survival phrases (greeting, asking for a recommendation, requesting the check, asking if they accept cards) 3 times each, timing each round and beating your first round by 5 seconds.
8.tip: You've earned a harder week — attack it with the same energy.

9.title: Day 9: Market Haggling Drill
activities: Record a 90-second market haggling dialogue where you offer a lower price, get countered twice, and agree on a final price.
Speak 15 market prices aloud using numbers 1-100 in under 60 seconds, then repeat the full set faster, beating your first time.
9.tip: Haggling fast builds the same muscle as real conversation — keep pushing the pace.

10.title: Day 10: Taxi and Transit Speed Round
activities: Record a 60-second conversation asking a taxi driver for directions to a hotel and confirming the fare out loud.
Practice 10 transportation phrases (bus schedule, platform number, buying a ticket) twice each, timing the full set and beating your first round by 10 seconds.
10.tip: Getting around smoothly in Spanish will make the trip feel effortless.

11.title: Day 11: Scenario Switching
activities: Record a 2-minute dialogue switching between a restaurant scene and a taxi scene without a script, using at least 10 words from the past 3 days.
Say 12 rapid question-answer pairs covering restaurant, market, and transportation topics, answering each within 3 seconds.
11.tip: Switching contexts fast is exactly what real travel conversations demand.

12.title: Day 12: Handling Complications
activities: Record a 90-second dialogue politely correcting a wrong restaurant order and requesting a replacement dish.
Respond out loud to 6 unexpected situations (lost ticket, delayed bus, no change available) in Spanish, each within 5 seconds.
12.tip: Handling surprises in Spanish is the mark of real fluency — you're closing in on it.

13.title: Day 13: Full Chain Run
activities: Record a continuous 3-minute dialogue covering ordering food, bargaining at a market stall, and asking a driver for directions, using zero English words.
Play back Day 8's recording next to today's recording, then record a 30-second spoken comparison in Spanish noting which one sounds smoother and faster.
13.tip: Stacking three scenes back-to-back shows how far your recall has come.

14.title: Day 14: Test — The Full Traveler Conversation
activities: Record one continuous 4-minute conversation in Spanish playing all three roles — restaurant customer, market shopper, and taxi passenger — start to finish, pausing no longer than 3 seconds at any point and using at least 20 vocabulary items from the past two weeks.
Time the recording and compare its length and hesitation count to Day 8's 60-second benchmark, aiming for under 4 minutes total with fewer than 5 hesitations.
14.tip: This is proof you can hold a real conversation in Mexico — run it with confidence.

8.title: Day 8: Restaurant Basics Refresh
activities: Write 5 Spanish restaurant phrases on a card (e.g. 'Quisiera...', 'Me trae la cuenta, por favor'), 5 minutes.
Say each of the 5 phrases aloud 3 times, using a timer for 8 minutes total.
Record yourself ordering one dish using 3 of the phrases, playback once, 5 minutes.
8.tip: Small steps this week — your brain is still filing last week's work.

9.title: Day 9: Market Vocabulary Warm-up
activities: Write 5 Spanish market phrases on a card (e.g. '¿Cuánto cuesta?', 'Es muy caro'), 5 minutes.
Say each of the 5 phrases aloud 3 times, 8 minutes with a timer.
Pick 2 phrases and act out buying a fruit with hand gestures, saying each once, 3 minutes.
9.tip: Easy reps today — you're building the base for faster recall later.

10.title: Day 10: Transportation Phrases
activities: Write 5 Spanish transportation phrases on a card (e.g. '¿Dónde está la parada de autobús?'), 5 minutes.
Say each phrase aloud 3 times, 8 minutes with a timer.
Record a 1-minute clip asking for directions to the bus stop, play it back once.
10.tip: One topic at a time keeps this manageable — nice work sticking with it.

11.title: Day 11: Speed Recall - Restaurant & Market
activities: Shuffle your restaurant and market cards, say 6 phrases aloud in under 2 minutes, repeat once.
Write a 4-line dialogue combining ordering food and asking the price, 6 minutes.
Visit a local Mexican restaurant or taquería and order one item in Spanish using 2 of your phrases.
11.tip: Real-world practice today — even one phrase used live counts as a win.

12.title: Day 12: Transportation Recall Drill
activities: Shuffle your transportation cards, say 6 phrases aloud in under 2 minutes, repeat once.
Practice asking about a taxi fare and a bus schedule, saying each phrase 2 times.
Record a 1-minute dialogue asking a stranger for directions to a bus stop.
12.tip: You're moving faster than you think — recall drills pay off quietly.

13.title: Day 13: Full Dialogue Rehearsal
activities: Write a 6-line dialogue mixing restaurant, market, and transportation phrases, 8 minutes.
Read the dialogue aloud 3 times, aiming for under 1 minute each read.
Flip through 5 flashcards from the week and say each answer once without reading notes.
13.tip: Tomorrow is the test — tonight's run-through is all you need.

14.title: Day 14: Mexico Trip Conversation Test
activities: Perform the 6-line dialogue from Day 13 start to finish in Spanish without reading, record it, 1 attempt.
Speak a 3-minute conversation covering ordering a meal, asking a market price, and asking for bus directions, recorded in one take.
Write the 3 phrases you paused on during the recording, one short list.
14.tip: Seven days ago this felt out of reach — now you can hold your own in Spanish.
